market_question: Ukraine agrees not to join NATO before 2027?
reasoning: The market's 17% implied probability likely underestimates the chance that Ukraine formally agrees to renounce NATO membership by end of 2026. With Trump's administration pushing for a ceasefire, a peace deal before 2027 is plausible, and Russia will make Ukrainian neutrality a condition. Ukraine's leadership, while publicly pro-NATO, may accept a temporary moratorium to secure peace and Western security guarantees, as seen in the 2022 Istanbul draft. I assess a 30% likelihood.
evidence_points: Trump is strongly pressuring for a Ukraine-Russia peace deal in 2025, raising odds of an agreement by the deadline.
Russia's core demand remains Ukraine's permanent neutrality and non-alignment; any peace deal will almost certainly include a NATO restriction.
During the 2022 Istanbul peace talks, Ukraine signaled willingness to adopt a neutral, non-nuclear status with international security guarantees, showing a precedent for such concessions.
Ukraine's de facto inability to join NATO soon (low membership odds, measured at ~6% by 2030 on Polymarket) reduces the political cost of formally agreeing not to join for a period.
sources_consulted: Polymarket odds on Ukraine joining NATO by 2030
News reports on Trump's peace initiatives (2025)
